ETag.description: The entity's version, the strong validator for `If-Match` (docs/adr/0050 D2)

ticket.description: The key of the ticket it waits on, when the caller can see that ticket

available.description: The members of the tenant may hold a conversation (POST …/chat)

The capabilities the chat's requests hold (docs/adr/0043 D5): what the chat may do beyond the

chosen.description:
The person chose the set; false is the default, every capability but decide, close, drop and
record-answer

capabilities.description: The whole set; an empty one leaves the chat the baseline

ChatDoneEvent.description: The data of a chat turn's event `done`, the last of every turn

messages.description: The messages the turn added, to be appended to the conversation as they are

ChatMessage.description:
One message of a conversation, in the neutral model the backend translates for its provider. A
`user` message carries `text`, what the person wrote; an `assistant` message `text`, what the model
said, and `tool_calls`, the calls it made — at least one of the two; a `tool` message
`tool_call_id`, the call it answers, `ok`, and `text`, the answer the model read. There is no
system message: the backend writes the model's instructions on every turn (docs/adr/0076).

ok.description: On a tool message, whether the call succeeded; a refusal of the API is a failure the model reads

ChatPageContext.description:
The page the person is on as they send the turn: the model's instructions name it, and a short
key the model uses resolves against its project

path.description: The page's path in this UI, without query or fragment, such as /t/acme/p/COW/board

project.description: The key of the project the page shows

ticket.description: The short key of the ticket the page shows, <PROJECT>-<number>

ChatProvider.description:
A provider the operator configured (COWORK_CHAT_PROVIDERS): what the person picks in the panel.
Its address and key are never shown

model.description: The model by the name its provider knows it (COWORK_CHAT_<ID>_MODEL)

name.description: The provider's name for the person (COWORK_CHAT_<ID>_NAME)

ChatProviderId.description: A configured provider's id, as COWORK_CHAT_PROVIDERS names it

ChatProviderKind.description:
The wire format a configured provider speaks (COWORK_CHAT_<ID>_KIND): OpenAI Chat Completions,
which OpenAI, LM Studio, Ollama and vLLM speak, or the Anthropic Messages API (docs/adr/0076)

ChatRole.description: Whom a message of the chat is from — the person, the model, or a tool answering the model

ChatTextEvent.description: The data of a chat turn's event `text`

delta.description: The next piece of the assistant's text, to be appended to the pieces before it

ChatToolArguments.description: A tool call's arguments as the model gave them, a JSON object; the tool's schema decides what they mean

ChatToolCall.description: A call of a tool the model made

id.description: The call's id, which the tool message answering it names

ChatToolResultEvent.description: The data of a chat turn's event `tool_result`

id.description: The id of the call it answers

ok.description: The call succeeded; false for a refusal of the API, which the model reads like any answer

summary.description:
The start of what the tool answered, Markdown as the tool wrote it, at most 2000 characters;
the whole answer is the text of the tool message in `done`

conversation.description:
The conversation's id, made by the client when the conversation begins and sent with each of
its turns; the agent mark of the tool calls carries it, so the activity tells one
conversation's acts from another's (docs/adr/0036 D3)

messages.description:
The conversation so far, oldest first: the person's messages and what the `done` events
added. It ends with the person's new message

ChatTurnEnd.description:
Why a turn ended: the model answered; the turn reached COWORK_CHAT_MAX_STEPS calls of the model,
and a new message goes on; the person stopped it (DELETE …/chat/turns); or an `error` event came
before

ChatUiAction.description: What a UI tool of the chat asks the client to do

ChatUiEvent.description: The data of a chat turn's event `ui`

path.description:
The page to show, a path of this UI in the turn's tenant: /t/<tenant>/tickets/<PROJECT>-<number>,
/t/<tenant>/p/<PROJECT>/backlog or /t/<tenant>/p/<PROJECT>/board

ChatUnavailableReason.description: Why the chat is not available — the installation configures no provider

group.description: The group's name as the identity provider's claim carries it, case and all, with no white space at either end

blocker.description: For `blocker_closed`, the ticket that blocked this one and reached done or dropped, as it is now; null otherwise

blocks one they watch reached done or dropped, an urgent stake on a ticket assigned to them

progress_review.description: The review stage, the work of review; derived like progress (docs/adr/0017 D2, D3)

note.description: The verification note done requires — what was run, against what, with what result (docs/adr/0009 D5)

override_prerequisites.description: Close over open prerequisites, with a reason; a person's act, never an agent's (docs/adr/0012 D7)

reason.description:
Required backward, into blocked (the block's text), to dropped, on a reopen, on the withdrawal of a
done by hand, and with override_prerequisites

Urgency.description: The ticket's horizon, a planning category a person or an agent sets in whatever state the ticket is (docs/adr/0010 D3)

reason.description: Null when a person set the override without one (docs/adr/0010 D3)
Optional for a person, required of an agent (docs/adr/0010 D3)

WipLimits.description:
Advisory work-in-progress limits per state; information, never a gate (docs/adr/0019 D3). The
board's Refinement column, which holds filed and analysed, counts against the analysed limit.

bearerToken.description:
A personal access token, `cwk_` and 43 base62 characters
(docs/adr/0035 D1). `X-Cowork-Agent: name/model/session` marks the
request as an agent's; a token with the agent flag is an agent's
with or without it, and no header removes the flag (docs/adr/0036).
A request that carries an `Authorization` header is a token's, and
its cookie, if any, is not looked at. A token of a person the identity
provider's groups no longer admit is refused with `401 not_allowed`,
checked against the person's groups as of their last login or groups
refresh, at most `COWORK_OIDC_GROUPS_REFRESH` apart, and so is one whose
groups are older than `COWORK_OIDC_GROUPS_MAX_AGE`, until the person
signs in to the browser once (docs/adr/0035 D8).

sessionCookie.description:
The session of a browser login: an opaque id of 256 random bits, set
by `POST /auth/local` or `GET /auth/callback` as `HttpOnly; Secure;
SameSite=Lax; Path=/` (docs/adr/0031 D2). A session acts as its
person with no agent flag and with the whole of the person's role: it
has no scope of its own. An `X-Cowork-Agent` header makes its request
an agent's — the capabilities the person chose for the chat
(`GET /api/v1/me/chat`), the agent rules, the mark on its acts — and
refuses it what only a session does with `403 agent_forbidden`
(docs/adr/0036 D3, docs/adr/0043 D5); the chat marks its tool calls so
(docs/adr/0076).
Its writes are held to the CSRF check of docs/adr/0037 D1: `Origin`
(or `Referer`) equal to the installation's `COWORK_BASE_URL` and
`X-Requested-With: cowork`.
sessionCookie.name: __Host-cowork-session

info.description:
A multi-tenant backlog for people and the agents that work for them.

Every route that names a person is authenticated with one of two
credentials. A personal access token, `Authorization: Bearer cwk_…`
(docs/adr/0035), is for scripts and agents; the session cookie of a
browser login (docs/adr/0031 — `POST /auth/local`, or the identity
provider's `GET /auth/callback`, docs/adr/0029) is for the UI. Each
operation says which it takes: most take either, a few a session only —
creating a token, a tenant or a local account, resetting or changing a
password, logging out, a turn of the chat and stopping one, choosing the
chat's capabilities, a global administrator's list of every tenant, and the
administration acts that give access: adding a member, setting a grant,
making or changing a group mapping, restricting or opening a project,
putting a person on its access list. A request of a session that writes must come from the installation's
origin and carry `X-Requested-With: cowork` (docs/adr/0037). A request
marked as an agent's — by the token's agent flag, or by an `X-Cowork-Agent:
name/model/session` header — is bound by the agent rules
(docs/adr/0036, 0043). Errors are RFC 9457 problem details with a stable
`code` (docs/adr/0047).
info.title: cowork

get.summary: The calling person and their tenants

get.description:
"Assigned to me" (docs/adr/0018 D3): every ticket that is neither `done` nor `dropped` and is
assigned to the person, in every tenant they belong to, each with its tenant — one read per
tenant (docs/adr/0021 D5), under the same predicate as the tenant's own lists. Ordered by the
tenant's slug, the project's key and the project's rank until the score of docs/adr/0014 D3
exists (D5). Cursor paging only (docs/adr/0048 D3); the cursor carries the rank sealed
(docs/adr/0014 D2). A token restricted to a tenant reads that tenant, one restricted to a
project that project (docs/adr/0035 D3).

200.description: A page of the person's tickets

get.summary: The open tickets assigned to the person, across their tenants

get.description:
The chat acts as the person's agent, and its requests hold exactly this set
(docs/adr/0043 D5, docs/adr/0076): an act that needs another capability is refused
to the chat with `403 agent_forbidden` and stays the person's. A person who never chose
holds the default — every capability but `decide`, `close`, `drop` and `record-answer` —,
and `chosen` is false.
get.summary: The capabilities the person gives the chat in the UI

put.description:
Only the person, in a browser session: what the chat may do is access to the person's
tenants, which a token does not give (`403 session_required`, docs/adr/0035 D5), and a session
the agent header marks — the chat itself among them — is `403 agent_forbidden`. The set
replaces the one before, from the chat's next request on, a running turn's included; an empty
set leaves the chat the baseline (docs/adr/0043 D4). No `If-Match`: the person is the only
writer, and the same set sent twice changes nothing (docs/adr/0050 D4). A change is recorded
as the person's act.
put.summary: Choose the capabilities the person gives the chat in the UI

get.description:
"Open decisions" (docs/adr/0018 D3): the open questions asked of the person and those open in
their tenants — asked of nobody (docs/adr/0011 D2) —, on tickets they see, each with its
tenant and its ticket; one read per tenant (docs/adr/0021 D5). Ordered by the tenant's slug,
the project's key, the ticket's place in the project's rank — a `done` or `dropped` ticket,
which has none, after the ranked ones — and the question's number, until the score exists
(docs/adr/0014 D5). Cursor paging only (docs/adr/0048 D3). A restricted token reads as on
`GET /api/v1/me/assigned`.

200.description: A page of the open decisions

get.summary: The open decisions of the person, across their tenants

get.description:
One inbox per person, a union over the tenants they belong to — one read per tenant, never one
query across them (docs/adr/0020 D1, docs/adr/0021 D5). A notification is written by the act
that caused it, for the events of docs/adr/0020 D2: a ticket assigned to the person, a
question asked of them, a question they asked answered, a state change of — or a comment on —
a ticket they watch (docs/adr/0013 D6: a stake, the assignee, the reporter, an open question
asked by or of them), a ticket that blocks one they watch reaching `done` or `dropped`, and an
`urgent` stake on a ticket assigned to them. Their own acts and their agents' tell them
nothing. Each entry names its tenant beside the ticket and renders from the act (D3): the
ticket as it is now, the act as the ticket's activity shows it — without its payload where
it names a ticket the person cannot see — and whether the comment or question it is on has
been withdrawn since. A notification of a ticket the person no longer sees, or of a tenant
they left, is absent and counts nowhere (docs/adr/0065 D5).

`unread` counts the person's unread notifications in the tenants the request reaches. A
token restricted to a tenant reads that tenant's, one restricted to a project that project's
(docs/adr/0035 D3). Cursor paging only; the cursor holds the place, so a notification that
arrives while the person reads shifts nothing (docs/adr/0048 D3).

200.description: A page of the inbox and the unread count

get.summary: The person's notifications across their tenants, newest first

put.description:
"Mark all read" (docs/adr/0020 D6): every unread notification of the person up to and
including `through`, in the tenants the request reaches; one that arrived after it stays
unread. One act `read` per tenant where something changed; none where nothing did. Needs
`write` scope. Read notifications are kept ninety days, unread ones until they are read.

200.description: The unread count after the marking

put.summary: Mark the person's notifications read, up to one they saw

put.description:
Recorded as the act `read`; one already read changes nothing and records nothing. A
notification that is not the person's, or of a ticket they no longer see, is `404 not_found`.
Needs `write` scope.

200.description: The unread count after the marking

put.summary: Mark one of the person's notifications read

put.description:
Needs the current password, which counts like a login attempt towards
the lockout of the account (docs/adr/0033 D6). The new one must be as long
as `COWORK_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH` and differ from the current one; every
other session of the account ends (D4), and a temporary password is no
longer temporary. The local administrator's password is set by the
configuration and cannot be changed here (`403 forbidden`).
put.summary: Change the password of the person's local account

get.description:
Normalises each `remote` to its identity, host/path (docs/adr/0066 D1), and
searches the projects the caller sees in every tenant of the person — a
restricted token in its own tenant and project only (docs/adr/0035 D3). The
remotes are tried in the order given, `origin` first by convention; the
first one with a binding decides, and of its bindings those whose
sub-directory covers `path`, the most specific first. One binding is
`bound`; several are `ambiguous`, a data error the person resolves
(docs/adr/0066 D6); none is `unbound`, with a proposal for a project made
from the first remote that has an identity (D2): the tenant — the only one
the caller may create projects in, else the one that binds repositories
under the same owner, else the list to choose from — a key from the
repository's name, free in each tenant offered, and the name itself. A
caller who may create a project nowhere gets no proposal and the reason.
A remote that names no host is reported with a null identity. Send no
credentials: cowork stores none, and a proxy's log may carry the query.

parameters.description: A git remote URL — SSH, scp-style, git or HTTP(S); repeatable, in order of preference
parameters.name: remote

parameters.name: path

get.description:
The token's metadata as the list shows it, the key of the project it is
restricted to, and the request's mark: whether it is an agent's — by the
token's flag or by an `X-Cowork-Agent` header (docs/adr/0036 D2, D3) — the
agent recorded on its acts, and the capabilities it holds
(docs/adr/0043 D4). The MCP server reads it at start to tell the model what
it may do (D6), and `cowork-mcp token check` to tell a person
(docs/adr/0070 D2). A browser session presents no token: `404 not_found`.
get.summary: The token this request presents, and what it makes of the request

get.description:
Metadata only; a token's plaintext is shown once, at creation
(docs/adr/0035 D1, D6). Newest first, paged by cursor, or by number with
a total (docs/adr/0048 D2).
get.summary: The person's tokens, revoked and expired ones included

post.description:
Only the person themselves, in a browser session: no token creates a
token (`403 session_required`) and no administrator creates one for
another person (docs/adr/0035 D5). The answer carries the plaintext
`token` once; cowork stores its SHA-256 only (D1).

The lifetime is `lifetime_days`, by default `COWORK_TOKEN_DEFAULT_LIFETIME`
(90 days) and at most `COWORK_TOKEN_MAX_LIFETIME` (one year): a longer
one is shortened to the maximum, and `expires_at` in the answer says what
the token got (D4). An agent token has at most `write` scope
(docs/adr/0036 D5), carries capabilities and nothing else does, and gets
every capability when `capabilities` is left out; an empty list is no
capability, the baseline only (docs/adr/0043 D4). A tenant
restriction needs a tenant the person belongs to, a project restriction a
project of it the person sees; either, if not, is `validation_failed`
without saying which of the two it was.

An `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry create nothing twice, but the stored
answer never holds the plaintext (docs/adr/0045 D6): the repetition
answers the token without `token`, and the person revokes it and makes
another.

201.description: The token, with its plaintext once

delete.description:
Immediate and recorded; the row stays listed (docs/adr/0035 D6). A
token may always revoke itself; revoking another token of the person
needs `write` scope, and an agent may revoke only the token it holds
(docs/adr/0043 D3). Revoking a revoked token changes nothing.
delete.summary: Revoke one of the person's tokens

get.description: Unauthenticated; `info.version` is the backend version (docs/adr/0046 D5).
get.summary: This document

get.description:
The optional binding file of a repository without a remote or of a fork
(docs/adr/0066 D4): `tenant` and `project`, and optionally `path` — the
sub-directory of a monorepo it binds — and `url`, the installation it
belongs to. Unauthenticated, so an editor can load it.
get.summary: The JSON Schema of a repository's `.cowork.yaml`

get.description:
Every tenant by slug, with the role the caller holds in it — the highest
of their mapping and their grant — or `null` where they hold none
(docs/adr/0034 D2). It is how a global administrator finds a tenant in
which they have no role: there they see its administration — the
tenant and its settings, its members, its group mappings — and grant
themselves a role (`PUT …/members/{person_id}/grant` with their own id),
and nothing of its work until they have. A person who is not a global
administrator is `403 forbidden`; the tenants they belong to are in
`GET /api/v1/me`. A browser session only, which no agent mark carries: a
token is `403 session_required`, so a leaked token of a global
administrator lists no tenant beyond the person's own.

200.description: A page of tenants, by slug

get.summary: Every tenant of the installation, for a global administrator

post.description:
A global administrator, in a browser session: no token creates a tenant
(`403 session_required`), and a person who is not a global administrator
is `403 forbidden`. The creator becomes the tenant's first administrator
by a marked grant, recorded with the tenant (docs/adr/0032 D7); a global
administrator has no other role in it (docs/adr/0034 D2). The slug is
immutable and never reused (docs/adr/0005 D4).

get.description:
Every member reads it; a global administrator who holds no role in the
tenant too, in a browser session, as part of its administration
(docs/adr/0034 D2).

An administrator's act with `admin` scope; agents never (docs/adr/0043 D3).
`If-Match` is required (docs/adr/0050 D3).

post.description:
The administrator sets a temporary password; the person changes it at the
first login, before anything else (docs/adr/0033 D4). The account gets a
marked grant with the given role in this tenant (docs/adr/0030 D3) and
is managed by this tenant. There is no registration and no invitation:
this route is the gate (D1). A username is unique in the installation,
so `409 username_taken` also tells an administrator that another tenant
has the name.

A browser session only: a token, an administrator's included, answers
`403 session_required`. An account made with a leaked token would
survive the token's revocation, and so would the password the
administrator chose.
post.summary: Create a local account in the tenant

put.description:
The person can no longer log in, their tokens are revoked and their
sessions end (docs/adr/0024 D5); the person and every act they made stay.
Not for the administrator's own account (`403 forbidden`). Deactivating a
deactivated account changes nothing. A deactivation that would leave the
tenant without an administrator who can log in is `409 last_admin` and
changes nothing (docs/adr/0034 D1); it takes the tenant's lock, so two
administrators who deactivate each other at once are decided one after
the other.
put.summary: Deactivate an account

delete.description:
Forgets the failed attempts and the lock of the username
(docs/adr/0033 D6). Not for the administrator's own account
(`403 forbidden`). Unlocking an account that is not locked changes
nothing.
delete.summary: Lift the lockout of an account

put.description:
The person must change it at the next login (docs/adr/0033 D5), and every
session of the account ends. Not for the administrator's own account: an
administrator changes theirs with `PUT /api/v1/me/password`, which asks
for the current one (`403 forbidden`).

A browser session only, like creating an account (`403 session_required`
for a token): a password reset with a leaked token would be access that
survives the token's revocation.
put.summary: Set a new temporary password

delete.description:
Immediate: the next request with such a session's cookie is
unauthenticated (docs/adr/0031 D4). Tokens are not affected.
delete.summary: End every session of an account

get.description:
Every attachment of the tenant counts, on every ticket, confidential ones and those of
restricted projects included — the sum the quota is checked against. The tenant's
administrators, a token's `read` scope; anybody else is `403 forbidden`, because the sum
counts files of tickets they may not see. `quota_bytes` is COWORK_ATTACHMENT_TENANT_QUOTA,
null where the installation sets none.
get.summary: The bytes the tenant's attachments hold, and the quota

get.description:
For the tenant's administrators. Filters combine with AND; a repeated
`action` with OR. Newest first, paged by cursor, or by number with a total
(docs/adr/0048 D2). `Accept: text/csv` returns the same rows as CSV, every
cell that could start a formula prefixed with an apostrophe. A CSV answer
carries no cursor: a client that reads more than one page as CSV asks for
numbered pages, with `to` held at the moment it began, so that a newer
row does not move the rows between two pages.

get.summary: The tenant's audit record (docs/adr/0026 D6)

get.description:
For every member of the tenant. The chat is available when the installation configures at
least one provider (`COWORK_CHAT_PROVIDERS`); `providers` lists them in the configured order,
the first being the one a turn uses when it names none. Otherwise `reason` says why. A
provider's address and key are never shown, and nothing here asks a provider whether it
answers: a turn that cannot reach it ends with an `error` event.

200.description: The chat's availability in the tenant

get.summary: Whether the chat is available in the tenant, and with which providers

post.description:
A person in a browser session, any member of the tenant: a token is `403 session_required` —
an agent with a token has the MCP server (docs/adr/0040) — and the CSRF check holds as for
every write of a session (docs/adr/0037). A tenant without the chat is `409
chat_unavailable`, and `GET …/chat` says why; a `provider` the installation does not configure
is `400 validation_failed`. A person with as many turns running as
`COWORK_CHAT_TURNS_PER_PERSON` allows on the replica — in another tab, say — is `429
chat_busy`. The backend keeps nothing between turns: the request carries the conversation,
and the answer the messages to append to it.

A turn runs the provider's model and the tools it calls: at most `COWORK_CHAT_MAX_STEPS` calls
of the model, for at most `COWORK_CHAT_TURN_TIMEOUT`. Every tool call is a request of this API
with the person's session, marked as the agent `chat/<model>/<conversation>`
(docs/adr/0036): it holds the capabilities the person chose for the chat (`GET
/api/v1/me/chat`, docs/adr/0043 D5), passes validation, authorization, the agent rules and the
audit like any agent's request, and what it changes reaches the event stream. It runs at once:
nothing waits for the person. It works in the turn's tenant only. A tool the API refuses — an
act that needs a capability the person did not give the chat is `403 agent_forbidden`
naming it — is an answer the model reads, not a failed turn. A call's creating requests carry
keys derived from the conversation and the call; a turn the model answers anew repeats its
acts: a client never retries one by itself.

The answer is `200` with `text/event-stream`, each event an `event:` line with its name and
a `data:` line with its JSON, flushed one by one:

- `text` — `ChatTextEvent`: the next piece of the assistant's text.
- `tool_call` — `ChatToolCall`: a call the model made, with its arguments, before it runs.
- `ui` — `ChatUiEvent`: between a call of `open_ticket`, `open_backlog` or `open_board` and its
  result, the page of this UI the client shows next.
- `tool_result` — `ChatToolResultEvent`: whether the call succeeded, and the start of what it
  answered the model.
- `error` — `Problem`: why the turn failed once it had begun — `chat_provider_failed`,
  `timeout` (`COWORK_CHAT_TURN_TIMEOUT`), `not_ready` (the server is shutting down: send
  the turn again), `internal`.
- `done` — `ChatDoneEvent`, always the last: the messages the turn added, to be appended to
  the conversation as they are, and why the turn ended — `stopped` when
  `DELETE …/chat/turns` ended it.

A `: keep-alive` comment follows ten seconds without an event, so no proxy closes a turn
while the model thinks. A stream that ends without `done` was cut — the network, the client's
abort, a shutdown —, and the acts its `tool_result` events reported have happened. A call
the turn's end left without an answer is answered to the model on the next turn as one
that did not run. An answer of the model that is white space only adds no message: `done`
carries none for it.

**Limits.** A body above `COWORK_MAX_JSON_BODY` is `413 payload_too_large`; more messages or
longer texts than `ChatTurn` allows are `400 validation_failed` — the conversation is too
long, and a new one begins. A message the model could not read in its place — a tool
message that answers no call, a conversation that does not end with the person's message —
is `400 validation_failed` naming it.

messages.text: File a bug for the login that fails in Safari, and rank it to now.

post.summary: One turn of the chat, answered as server-sent events

delete.description:
A person in a browser session, any member: a token is `403 session_required`, a session the
agent header marks `403 agent_forbidden`, and the CSRF check holds. Every turn of the
session's person in the tenant that runs on the replica answering this request ends at once:
its call of the model is cancelled, so is a tool call in flight, and its stream ends with
`done` and the reason `stopped`. The answer comes once those turns have ended, or after five
seconds; a turn of another person, or of the person in another tenant, runs on. What the
stopped turns' tool calls did before has happened.

The turns are those of this replica (docs/adr/0076): behind several backend replicas a turn
another replica runs is not reached — the client's abort of the turn's own request still is.
With no turn running, nothing happens, and the answer is the same.

204.description: The person's turns in the tenant on this replica are stopped

delete.summary: Stop every running turn of the person in the tenant

get.description:
`ticket.changed` (an upload included), `comment.changed`, `question.changed`,
`link.changed` and `interest.changed`, each with `data: {"key", "version", "kind"}` — a key
and a version, never content (docs/adr/0054 D2); `id:` is the act's id. An event of a
project the caller cannot see, or of a confidential ticket they may not read, never
arrives (D3).

`membership.changed` says that who belongs to the tenant, or who sees a project, changed —
by an administrator's act or by the identity provider's groups (docs/adr/0030 D2, D6). Its
`data` carries keys only, each where it applies: `person_id`, the person whose membership
or project access changed; `project_id`, the project whose restriction or access list
changed; `mapping_id`, the group mapping made, changed or removed. The client reloads what
it shows of members, mappings and access lists, its project list when `project_id` is
there, and the person's own `GET /api/v1/me`. An event about an access entry reaches the
tenant's administrators and the person it names, one about a mapping the administrators,
every other every member.

With `me=true` — the person-level pages, and the bell in the top bar — the stream also carries
the person's own events across every tenant they belong to (docs/adr/0054 D1):
`inbox.changed` with `data: {"unread": n}`, the person's unread notifications in every tenant
the request reaches (`GET /api/v1/me/inbox` counts the same), sent when the stream opens and
whenever the inbox changes — a notification for them, or theirs marked read —; and
`question.changed` of a question asked of them in another tenant, which arrives only while
they are a member of that tenant and see its ticket, as the tenant's own stream would judge
it. Neither carries an `id:` or is replayed: the count says how things stand, and the client
reloads its person-level lists when the stream opens. A token restricted to a tenant hears
nothing of another (docs/adr/0035 D3).

A reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` inside the replay window replays the gap;
beyond it the stream starts with `event: resync`, and the client refetches its lists (D5).
A comment every twenty seconds keeps proxies open and checks the token and the
membership again; the stream ends when either fails. `event: unavailable` ends a stream
the server closes — the person's eleventh, a shutdown — and the client polls (D7, D8).

parameters.description: The id of the last event the client received
parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

parameters.description: Adds the person's own events across their tenants (docs/adr/0054 D1)
parameters.name: me

get.summary: The tenant's events the caller may see, as server-sent events

get.description:
Each mapping gives its role to every person whose groups include its
group; several matches yield the highest role (docs/adr/0030 D2).
`includes_caller` says the calling person is one of them, so the editor
can warn before a change takes the editor's own role away. The tenant's
administrators read them, and a global administrator who holds no role
in the tenant, in a browser session (docs/adr/0034 D2).
get.summary: The tenant's group mappings, by group

post.description:
The group is matched exactly, case and all, against the groups the
identity provider's claim carries (docs/adr/0029 D2). The mapping applies
at once to every person whose groups, as of their last login or groups
refresh, include it: their memberships are derived in the same
transaction, recorded with the cause `mapping`. Everyone else is caught
up at their next login or groups refresh (docs/adr/0030 D5). A group the
tenant maps already is `409 mapping_exists`.

Only a global administrator who administers the tenant maps a group, in
a browser session; any other administrator of the tenant is
`403 forbidden`, and nothing is written. Every tenant shares the identity
provider's one namespace of groups, and a mapping admits everyone in its
group at once (docs/adr/0030 D7).
post.summary: Map a group of the identity provider to a role

delete.description:
The memberships it derived go at once, or fall to the highest of the
person's other mapped groups; grants stay (docs/adr/0030 D3). Any
administrator of the tenant may remove one, with an `admin`-scope token
too: it only takes access away (docs/adr/0030 D7).
Idempotent: removing a mapping that does not exist answers 204 as well.

patch.description:
`If-Match` is required (docs/adr/0050 D3). The memberships the mapping
derives change at once, as at its creation. Like its creation, a global
administrator's who administers the tenant: any other administrator is
`403 forbidden` (docs/adr/0030 D7).

get.description:
Each member with the effective role — the higher of the mapped and the
granted one (docs/adr/0030 D4) — and `origins`, every source with its
own role; `local` marks a person with a local account rather than an
identity of the identity provider (docs/adr/0033). `email` is the
address that tells two persons of one name apart, for the tenant's

get.description:
Where the issuer sends the browser back: `COWORK_BASE_URL` +
`/auth/callback`, the redirect URI registered with the identity
provider (docs/adr/0029 D4). The UI never calls it.

The state cookie of `GET /auth/oidc/login` must be present, younger than
ten minutes, and hold the `state` the issuer returned. The code is
exchanged with the PKCE verifier; the ID token's signature, issuer,
audience, expiry and nonce are verified (D1); the groups are read from
`COWORK_OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM` — in the ID token, else from UserInfo (D2) —
and must pass the gate: one of them is in `COWORK_OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUPS` or
is `COWORK_ADMIN_GROUP` (docs/adr/0030 D1). The person is found by
issuer and subject, or made (docs/adr/0029 D5), and their memberships
are derived from the tenants' group mappings (docs/adr/0030 D2). Then the
session is made as the local login makes it — a new cookie, and the
session the request presented ended (docs/adr/0031 D5) — the state
cookie is cleared, and the answer is `303` to `return_to`.

Every failure is `303` to `/login?error=<code>&return=<return_to>`, the
state cookie cleared and no session made. `return` is the path the login
began with, for the page's next attempt: it is there when the state
cookie still opens, stale or not, and the path is not `/`, the page's
default. The codes: `oidc_failed` — the state cookie is missing, stale
or does not match, the exchange or the verification failed, or the
issuer answered with `error`; `not_allowed` — the person is outside the
gate, or deactivated (docs/adr/0024 D5); `not_initialised` — no tenant
exists and the person is not in `COWORK_ADMIN_GROUP` (docs/adr/0032 D5);
`oidc_unavailable` — no identity provider is configured. A refused
login is recorded (docs/adr/0026); the reason reaches the log, never the
page, and neither ever holds a code or a token.

The issuer may add parameters this document does not name, such as `iss`
(RFC 9207) or `session_state`: the route takes them and reads none of
them (`x-cowork-open-query`).

parameters.description: The issuer's error, sent instead of `code` (RFC 6749 4.1.2.1)

post.description:
Sets the session cookie `__Host-cowork-session` (`HttpOnly; Secure;
SameSite=Lax; Path=/`) and answers whether the password is temporary
and must be changed before anything else (docs/adr/0033 D4). A new
session is made at every login, and the one the request presented is
ended (docs/adr/0031 D5).

Every failure is the same `401 invalid_credentials` in the same time —
an unknown username, a wrong password, a locked or a deactivated
account — so neither the answer nor the lockout says whether an account
exists (docs/adr/0033 D6). `COWORK_LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES` (5) failures of one
username within fifteen minutes lock it; more attempts from one client
address within a minute than `COWORK_LOGIN_ADDRESS_LIMIT` (20) allows are
`429 too_many_attempts` — the client being the TCP peer, or behind
`COWORK_TRUSTED_PROXIES` the first address of `X-Forwarded-For`, from the
right, that is not one of them (docs/adr/0035 D2). While no
tenant exists, only a global administrator may log in: anyone else, with
the right password, gets `403 not_initialised` and no session
(docs/adr/0032 D5).

There is no session yet to carry a CSRF check, so the request must come
from `COWORK_BASE_URL`: its `Origin`, or without one its `Referer`, has
to equal it, else `403 csrf` (docs/adr/0037 D5).

browser goes next to end its session at the issuer as well (D4). The
ID token was not kept (D1), so the URL carries no `id_token_hint`. Every
other logout answers `204`.

`__Host-cowork-oidc` that holds them with `return_to` for the callback.
Without one, or while its gate admits nobody — the cases in which
`GET /auth/options` answers `oidc: false` — it is `303` to
`/login?error=oidc_unavailable&return=<return_to>`.

`return_to` is where the browser lands after the login: a path of this
installation that starts with `/`, not with `//` or `/\`, holds no
control character and is at most 2048 characters long. Anything else,
or none, is `/`; it is never refused, so a bad link still leads to a
login.

No credential: whoever comes here has none yet. Nothing is decided here
that a forged link could abuse — the session is made by the callback,
and only for the browser that holds the state cookie this answer set.

The local form is offered when at least one active local account exists
(docs/adr/0033 D8); the identity provider's button, "Sign in with
`oidc_name`", when one is configured and its gate admits somebody —
`COWORK_OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUPS` or `COWORK_ADMIN_GROUP` names a group
(docs/adr/0030 D1, D8). The minimum password length is the policy every
password form follows (docs/adr/0033 D3), and the longest lifetime of a
new token the bound of the token form (docs/adr/0035 D4) — the policies
of the installation, public like the rest of this answer.
